title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 56 (Transfer and Transmission of Securities)

content.overview: Section 56 governs transfer and transmission of securities, proper transfer instruments and timing, partly-paid share notice, delivery of certificates, public-company transferability, and penalties for default.
content.glance: Section 56 governs transfer and transmission of securities, proper transfer instruments and timing, partly-paid share notice, delivery of certificates, public-company transferability, and penalties for default.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 56 (Transfer and transmission of securities). For a transfer, the company generally must receive a proper prescribed instrument, duly stamped, dated and executed, with the required particulars and certificate, within 60 days of execution. A lost or undelivered instrument may be dealt with on indemnity terms the Board thinks fit. Transfer between persons both recorded as beneficial owners in depository records is treated under the statutory exception. Transmission by operation of law is distinct and does not require the same transfer instrument. If a transferor alone applies to transfer partly paid shares, notice must be given to the transferee, who has two weeks after receipt to object. A public company's securities are generally freely transferable, subject to applicable law and enforceable contractual arrangements. Section 56 sets certificate-delivery periods: two months from incorporation for subscribers, two months from allotment for shares, one month from receipt of transfer/transmission papers, and six months from allotment for debentures; for dematerialised securities, the company must intimate allotment details to the depository immediately. A legal representative's transfer is valid as if the representative had been the holder when executing the instrument. Subsection (6) provides current penalties for non-compliance, and subsection (7) addresses fraudulent transfers by a depository/depository participant. Check current rules and dematerialisation requirements for the transaction.

sections.heading: Transfer instrument and 60-day delivery
sections.body: A company generally must not register a transfer unless a prescribed instrument, duly stamped, dated and executed by/on behalf of transferor and transferee, with the prescribed transferee particulars, is delivered within 60 days of execution along with the certificate. The section provides an indemnity route where the instrument is lost or not delivered in time.

sections.heading: Depository records and transmission
sections.body: The instrument requirement has a statutory exception for transfers between persons both recorded as beneficial owners in depository records. Transmission by operation of law is distinct from a voluntary transfer and may be registered on receipt of the required intimation.

sections.heading: Partly paid shares
sections.body: Where the transferor alone applies to transfer partly paid shares, the company must notify the transferee as prescribed; the transferee may object within two weeks after receiving notice.

sections.heading: Public-company transferability
sections.body: Securities or other member interests in a public company are freely transferable, subject to the Act. Any contract or arrangement between persons concerning transfer is enforceable as a contract, subject to applicable law.

sections.heading: Certificate-delivery deadlines
sections.body: Certificates are due within two months from incorporation for subscribers, two months from allotment for shares, one month from receipt of transfer/transmission papers, and six months from allotment for debentures. For securities dealt with in a depository, allotment details must be intimated immediately.

sections.heading: Legal representative and penalties
sections.body: A transfer by a deceased person's legal representative is valid as if the representative had been the holder when executing the instrument. Subsection (6) sets penalties for default in subsections (1)–(5); subsection (7) addresses fraudulent transfer by a depository or participant. Apply the current amended wording.

examples.title: Valid transfer
examples.body: A duly stamped and executed transfer form is delivered with the share certificate within sixty days. The company may register the transfer under s. 56.

examples.title: Transmission on death
examples.body: On the death of a member, the legal representative seeks registration by transmission. No instrument of transfer is required under s. 56.

hypotheticals.question: A physical transfer instrument was executed 70 days ago and delivered today. What issue arises?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 56 generally requires delivery within 60 days of execution. Check whether the instrument was lost or not delivered in time and whether the Board can register on indemnity terms under the section.

hypotheticals.question: A transferor alone applies to transfer partly paid shares. What notice protection applies?
hypotheticals.analysis: The company must give prescribed notice to the transferee, who may object within two weeks after receipt.

hypotheticals.question: When must a company deliver a share certificate after transfer papers are received?
hypotheticals.analysis: The statutory period is one month from receipt of the instrument of transfer or intimation of transmission, unless a legal prohibition or order applies.

misconceptions.trap: Treating transfer and transmission as the same process.
misconceptions.correction: Transfer generally involves the prescribed instrument; transmission arises by operation of law and is handled under the separate statutory route.

misconceptions.trap: Applying the physical-instrument rule identically to dematerialised holdings.
misconceptions.correction: Check the statutory depository-record exception and current dematerialisation rules.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the partly-paid share notice and two-week objection period.
misconceptions.correction: Where the transferor alone applies for partly paid shares, the transferee receives prescribed notice and may object within two weeks.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the ordinary deadline for delivery of a transfer instrument?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Within 60 days from execution, with the required certificate, subject to the section's exceptions.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What are the certificate-delivery periods?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Two months from incorporation for subscribers; two months from allotment for shares; one month from receipt of transfer/transmission papers; and six months from allotment for debentures.
